Verdict

No confirmed indicators of a malicious supply-chain compromise were identified. Overall risk: info.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • pyproject.toml uses the standard hatchling.build backend, and there is no evidence of malicious install-time or build-time hooks in the provided content.
  • No .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, or setup.py automatic execution files were observed in the provided extracted text.
  • [project.scripts] dockerwiz = "dockerwiz.cli:main" is a normal console_scripts entry point and requires the user to run the dockerwiz command. It is not evidence of execution during installation or interpreter startup.
  • Docker Hub queries, Docker command wrappers, and debug logging in dockerwiz/cli.py appear tied to user-invoked CLI commands, not automatic execution.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • Credential harvesting: no evidence of broad discovery of environment variables, SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI tokens, wallets, or shell history files.
  • Archive staging / exfiltration: no evidence of harvested-file compression, staging, webhook upload, C2 endpoint, raw IP endpoint, or paste/drop-service upload.
  • Persistence: no evidence of cron jobs, systemd units, launch agents, shell profile modification, startup-folder registration, or background polling loops.
  • Lateral movement: no evidence involving Kubernetes service-account tokens, Docker socket abuse, cloud metadata access, GitHub Actions token theft, or workflow injection.
  • Obfuscation/loader: re.compile usage appears to be ordinary tag filtering/input validation. No evidence of eval/exec/compile, base64/zlib/marshal loaders, or obfuscated payloads was identified.
  • Network access is consistent with the package’s documented Docker Hub API functionality (https://hub.docker.com/...), with no evidence of attacker-controlled exfiltration endpoints.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Hidden-path files such as .github/workflows/*, .gitignore, .claude/settings.local.json, and template .dockerignore.j2/.env.example.j2 files are included in the sdist. Based on the provided content, they do not show executable payloads or malicious supply-chain behavior.
  • docs/images/dockerwiz_new.png appears to be a PNG image binary; the provided evidence does not indicate a hidden executable payload.
  • Dependencies in pyproject.toml generally match the expected functionality of a CLI/TUI Docker scaffolding tool. No evidence of suspicious dependency insertion was identified.
  • Wheel/sdist mismatch could not be assessed from the provided sdist-focused materials.

Additional Verification Needed

  • Only selected text from 18 of 90 extracted files was provided, so static review of unprovided files is limited.
  • Binary files such as PNG images were not analyzed for steganography or hidden payloads from the text corpus alone.
  • If a wheel artifact exists for the same version, compare it against the sdist for file or behavior mismatches.
